test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: India launched the 'National Social Assistance Programme' in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) was launched by the Government of India in August 1995.
 
• It aims to provide financial assistance to the elderly, widows, and persons with disabilities in the form of social pensions.
 
• NSAP is a centrally sponsored scheme that comes under the Ministry of Rural Development.
 
• The programme includes schemes like the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), and Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS).
 
• The NSAP aims to ensure minimum national standards for social assistance in addition to the benefits that states are currently providing or might provide in the future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)**

 
 
• This scheme provides a monthly pension to elderly individuals who are 60 years or older and belong to below poverty line (BPL) households.
 
• As of recent guidelines, the central government provides Rs. 200 per month for beneficiaries aged 60-79 years and Rs. 500 per month for those aged 80 years and above.
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS)**
 
 
• Under this scheme, widows aged 40-59 years and belonging to BPL households receive a monthly pension of Rs. 300 from the central government.
 
• Many states provide additional amounts on top of the central contribution.
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS)**
 
 
• This scheme is designed for individuals aged 18-59 years with severe disabilities and belonging to BPL households.
 
• The central government provides Rs. 300 per month, and states may add more to this amount.
 
 
 
• **Annapurna Scheme**
 
 
• The Annapurna Scheme provides 10 kg of free food grains per month to BPL senior citizens who are not covered under IGNOAPS.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria**
 
 
• The primary eligibility criteria for all NSAP schemes are that the beneficiaries must belong to BPL households.
 
• State governments are responsible for identifying and verifying the beneficiaries under these schemes.
